verses.pali: Saṁyutta Nikāya 54.10
verses.english: Linked Discourses 54.10

verses.pali: 1. Ekadhammavagga
verses.english: 1. One Thing

verses.pali: Kimilasutta
verses.english: With Kimbila

verses.pali: Evaṁ me sutaṁ—
verses.english: So I have heard.

verses.pali: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā kimilāyaṁ viharati veḷuvane.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying near Kimbilā in the Freshwater Mangrove Wood.

verses.pali: Tatra kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ kimilaṁ āmantesi:
verses.english: Then the Buddha said to Venerable Kimbila,

verses.pali: “kathaṁ bhāvito nu kho, kimila, ānāpānassatisamādhi kathaṁ bahulīkato mahapphalo hoti mahānisaṁso”ti?
verses.english: “Kimbila, how is immersion due to mindfulness of breathing developed and cultivated so that it is very fruitful and beneficial?”

verses.pali: Evaṁ vutte, āyasmā kimilo tuṇhī ahosi.
verses.english: When he said this, Kimbila kept silent.

verses.pali: Dutiyampi kho bhagavā …pe…
verses.english: For a second time …

verses.pali: tatiyampi kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ kimilaṁ āmantesi:
verses.english: And for a third time, the Buddha said to him,

verses.pali: “kathaṁ bhāvito nu kho, kimila, ānāpānassatisamādhi kathaṁ bahulīkato mahapphalo hoti mahānisaṁso”ti?
verses.english: “How is immersion due to mindfulness of breathing developed and cultivated so that it is very fruitful and beneficial?”

verses.pali: Tatiyampi kho āyasmā kimilo tuṇhī ahosi.
verses.english: And a second time and a third time Kimbila kept silent.

verses.pali: Evaṁ vutte, āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: When he said this, Venerable Ānanda said to the Buddha,

verses.pali: “etassa, bhagavā, kālo; etassa, sugata, kālo.
verses.english: “Now is the time, Blessed One! Now is the time, Holy One!

verses.pali: Yaṁ bhagavā ānāpānassatisamādhiṁ bhāseyya, bhagavato sutvā bhikkhū dhāressantī”ti.
verses.english: Let the Buddha speak on immersion due to mindfulness of breathing. The mendicants will listen and remember it.”

verses.pali: “Tenahānanda, suṇāhi, sādhukaṁ manasi karohi; bhāsissāmī”ti.
verses.english: “Well then, Ānanda, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

verses.pali: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi.
verses.english: “Yes, sir,” Ānanda replied.

verses.pali: Bhagavā etadavoca:
verses.english: The Buddha said this:

verses.pali: “kathaṁ bhāvito ca, ānanda, ānāpānassatisamādhi kathaṁ bahulīkato mahapphalo hoti mahānisaṁso?
verses.english: “Ānanda, how is immersion due to mindfulness of breathing developed and cultivated so that it is very fruitful and beneficial?

verses.pali: Idhānanda, bhikkhu araññagato vā rukkhamūlagato vā suññāgāragato vā nisīdati pallaṅkaṁ ābhujitvā ujuṁ kāyaṁ paṇidhāya parimukhaṁ satiṁ upaṭṭhapetvā.
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant—gone to a wilderness, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty hut—sits down cross-legged, sets their body straight, and brings mindfulness to the present.

verses.pali: So satova assasati, satova passasati …pe…
verses.english: Just mindful, they breathe in. Mindful, they breathe out. …

verses.pali: ‘paṭinissaggānupassī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘paṭinissaggānupassī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati.
verses.english: They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe in observing letting go.’ They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe out observing letting go.’

verses.pali: Evaṁ bhāvito kho, ānanda, ānāpānassatisamādhi evaṁ bahulīkato mahapphalo hoti mahānisaṁso.
verses.english: That’s how immersion due to mindfulness of breathing, when developed and cultivated, is very fruitful and beneficial.

verses.pali: Yasmiṁ samaye, ānanda, bhikkhu dīghaṁ vā assasanto ‘dīghaṁ assasāmī’ti pajānāti, dīghaṁ vā passasanto ‘dīghaṁ passasāmī’ti pajānāti;
verses.english: There’s a time when a mendicant is breathing in heavily, and they know: ‘I’m breathing in heavily.’ Breathing out heavily they know: ‘I’m breathing out heavily.’

verses.pali: rassaṁ vā assasanto ‘rassaṁ assasāmī’ti pajānāti, rassaṁ vā passasanto ‘rassaṁ passasāmī’ti pajānāti;
verses.english: When breathing in lightly they know: ‘I’m breathing in lightly.’ Breathing out lightly they know: ‘I’m breathing out lightly.’

verses.pali: ‘sabbakāyappaṭisaṁvedī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘sabbakāyappaṭisaṁvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati;
verses.english: They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe in experiencing the whole body.’ They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe out experiencing the whole body.’

verses.pali: ‘passambhayaṁ kāyasaṅkhāraṁ assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘passambhayaṁ kāyasaṅkhāraṁ passasissāmī’ti sikkhati—
verses.english: They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe in stilling the physical process.’ They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe out stilling the physical process.’

verses.pali: kāye kāyānupassī, ānanda, bhikkhu tasmiṁ samaye viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ.
verses.english: At such a time a mendicant is meditating by observing an aspect of the body—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

verses.pali: Taṁ kissa hetu?
verses.english: Why is that?

verses.pali: Kāyaññatarāhaṁ, ānanda, etaṁ vadāmi yadidaṁ—assāsapassāsaṁ.
verses.english: Because the breath is a certain aspect of the body, I say.

verses.pali: Tasmātihānanda, kāye kāyānupassī bhikkhu tasmiṁ samaye viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ.
verses.english: Therefore, at such a time a mendicant is meditating by observing an aspect of the body—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

verses.pali: Yasmiṁ samaye, ānanda, bhikkhu ‘pītippaṭisaṁvedī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘pītippaṭisaṁvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati;
verses.english: There’s a time when a mendicant practices like this: ‘I’ll breathe in experiencing rapture.’ They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe out experiencing rapture.’

verses.pali: ‘sukhappaṭisaṁvedī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘sukhappaṭisaṁvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati;
verses.english: They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe in experiencing bliss.’ They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe out experiencing bliss.’

verses.pali: ‘cittasaṅkhārappaṭisaṁvedī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘cittasaṅkhārappaṭisaṁvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati;
verses.english: They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe in experiencing the the mental process.’ They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe out experiencing the the mental process.’

verses.pali: ‘passambhayaṁ cittasaṅkhāraṁ passasissāmī’ti sikkhati—
verses.english: They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe in stilling the mental process.’ They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe out stilling the mental process.’

verses.pali: vedanāsu vedanānupassī, ānanda, bhikkhu tasmiṁ samaye viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ.
verses.english: At such a time a mendicant is meditating by observing an aspect of feelings—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

verses.pali: Taṁ kissa hetu?
verses.english: Why is that?

verses.pali: Vedanāññatarāhaṁ, ānanda, etaṁ vadāmi, yadidaṁ—assāsapassāsānaṁ sādhukaṁ manasikāraṁ.
verses.english: Because careful application of mind to the in-breaths and out-breaths is a certain aspect of feelings, I say.

verses.pali: Tasmātihānanda, vedanāsu vedanānupassī bhikkhu tasmiṁ samaye viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ.
verses.english: Therefore, at such a time a mendicant is meditating by observing an aspect of feelings—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

verses.pali: Yasmiṁ samaye, ānanda, bhikkhu ‘cittappaṭisaṁvedī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘cittappaṭisaṁvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati;
verses.english: There’s a time when a mendicant practices like this: ‘I’ll breathe in experiencing the mind.’ They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe out experiencing the mind.’

verses.pali: abhippamodayaṁ cittaṁ …pe…
verses.english: They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe in gladdening the mind.’ They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe out gladdening the mind.’

verses.pali: samādahaṁ cittaṁ …
verses.english: They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe in immersing the mind in samādhi.’ They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe out immersing the mind in samādhi.’

verses.pali: ‘vimocayaṁ cittaṁ assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘vimocayaṁ cittaṁ passasissāmī’ti sikkhati—
verses.english: They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe in freeing the mind.’ They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe out freeing the mind.’

verses.pali: citte cittānupassī, ānanda, bhikkhu tasmiṁ samaye viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ.
verses.english: At such a time a mendicant is meditating by observing an aspect of the mind—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

verses.pali: Taṁ kissa hetu?
verses.english: Why is that?

verses.pali: Nāhaṁ, ānanda, muṭṭhassatissa asampajānassa ānāpānassatisamādhibhāvanaṁ vadāmi.
verses.english: Because there is no development of immersion due to mindfulness of breathing for someone who is unmindful and lacks awareness, I say.

verses.pali: Tasmātihānanda, citte cittānupassī bhikkhu tasmiṁ samaye viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ.
verses.english: Therefore, at such a time a mendicant is meditating by observing an aspect of the mind—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

verses.pali: Yasmiṁ samaye, ānanda, bhikkhu ‘aniccānupassī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati …pe…
verses.english: There’s a time when a mendicant practices like this: ‘I’ll breathe in observing impermanence.’ They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe out observing impermanence.’

verses.pali: virāgānupassī …
verses.english: They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe in observing fading away.’ They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe out observing fading away.’

verses.pali: nirodhānupassī …
verses.english: They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe in observing cessation.’ They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe out observing cessation.’

verses.pali: ‘paṭinissaggānupassī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘paṭinissaggānupassī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati—
verses.english: They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe in observing letting go.’ They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe out observing letting go.’

verses.pali: dhammesu dhammānupassī, ānanda, bhikkhu tasmiṁ samaye viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ.
verses.english: At such a time a mendicant is meditating by observing an aspect of principles—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

verses.pali: So yaṁ taṁ hoti abhijjhādomanassānaṁ pahānaṁ taṁ paññāya disvā sādhukaṁ ajjhupekkhitā hoti.
verses.english: Having seen with wisdom the giving up of covetousness and displeasure, they watch closely over with equanimity.

verses.pali: Tasmātihānanda, dhammesu dhammānupassī bhikkhu tasmiṁ samaye viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ.
verses.english: Therefore, at such a time a mendicant is meditating by observing an aspect of principles—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi, ānanda, catumahāpathe mahāpaṁsupuñjo.
verses.english: Suppose there was a large heap of sand at the crossroads.

verses.pali: Puratthimāya cepi disāyaṁ āgaccheyya sakaṭaṁ vā ratho vā, upahanateva taṁ paṁsupuñjaṁ;
verses.english: And a cart or chariot were to come by from the east,

verses.pali: pacchimāya cepi disāya āgaccheyya …
verses.english: west,

verses.pali: uttarāya cepi disāya …
verses.english: north,

verses.pali: dakkhiṇāya cepi disāya āgaccheyya sakaṭaṁ vā ratho vā, upahanateva taṁ paṁsupuñjaṁ.
verses.english: or south and destroy that heap of sand.

verses.pali: Evameva kho, ānanda, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharantopi upahanateva pāpake akusale dhamme;
verses.english: In the same way, when a mendicant is meditating by observing an aspect of the body,

verses.pali: vedanāsu …pe…
verses.english: feelings,

verses.pali: citte …pe…
verses.english: mind,

verses.pali: dhammesu dhammānupassī viharantopi upahanateva pāpake akusale dhamme”ti.
verses.english: or principles, they destroy bad, unskillful qualities.”

verses.pali: Dasamaṁ.
Ekadhammavaggo paṭhamo.
Tassuddānaṁ
Ekadhammo ca bojjhaṅgo,
suddhikañca duve phalā;
Ariṭṭho kappino dīpo,
vesālī kimilena cāti.
